title: Peter Pan
author: J. M. Barrie
ru: Мальчик, который не хочет взрослеть, уносит Венди и её братьев в Нетландию — к феям, русалкам и пиратам капитана Крюка.

chapters.title: Chapter 1. The Boy at the Window
chapters.text:
All children grow up, except one. This is the story of that one boy.

The Darling family lived in a house in London. There were Mr and Mrs Darling and their three children: Wendy, John and Michael. Wendy was the oldest. The family was not rich, so their nurse was a big dog. Her name was Nana. She was a very good nurse. She gave the children their baths and took them to school every day.

Every night Mrs Darling sat in the nursery and told the children stories. And every night someone else listened at the window. It was a boy. He loved stories, especially stories about Cinderella.

One night Mrs Darling fell asleep in her chair near the fire. Suddenly the window opened, and a strange boy flew into the room. He was dressed in leaves, and he still had all his first teeth. With him there was a little ball of light. It was moving around the room very fast.

Mrs Darling woke up and screamed. At that moment, Nana ran in. She jumped at the boy. The boy flew out of the window quickly, but Nana closed the window with her teeth. She caught the boy's shadow, and it came off!

Mrs Darling looked at the shadow. It was just an ordinary shadow. She rolled it up carefully and put it in a drawer.

“He is going to come back for it,” she thought. She was worried, but she didn't tell anybody about the boy.

A week later, Mr and Mrs Darling went to a party. Mr Darling was angry with Nana that evening, so he tied her up in the yard. The children were alone in the nursery with only three night-lights.

chapters.title: Chapter 2. Peter Finds His Shadow
chapters.text:
That night, the little ball of light came back through the window. It was a fairy, and her name was Tinker Bell. She was not bigger than your hand. When she spoke, it sounded like little golden bells.

A moment later, the boy flew in after her. “Tink, where is my shadow?” he whispered.

Tinker Bell showed him the drawer. The boy opened it and took out his shadow. He was very happy, but then he had a problem. How could he put it on again? He tried to stick it on with soap. It didn't work. He sat on the floor and started to cry.

His crying woke Wendy. She sat up in bed. She wasn't afraid. She was only interested.

“Boy,” she said kindly, “why are you crying?”

He stood up and bowed to her beautifully. She bowed back from the bed.

“What's your name?” he asked.

“Wendy Moira Angela Darling,” she answered proudly. “What's yours?”

“Peter Pan.”

“Where do you live?”

“Second to the right,” said Peter, “and then straight on till morning.”

“What a funny address!” said Wendy.

Then she saw the problem with the shadow. “I can sew it on for you,” she said. She took her sewing bag and sewed the shadow to his feet. It hurt a little, but Peter didn't cry. Soon he was dancing around the room with his shadow.

“How clever I am!” he shouted.

“You're not clever, I did it!” said Wendy.

“I ran away on the day I was born,” said Peter. “I heard my parents talking about my future. I don't want to be a man. I want to be a little boy for ever and have fun. So I live with the fairies now, in Neverland.”

chapters.title: Chapter 3. Come Away to Neverland
chapters.text:
Wendy was very excited. “You know fairies!” she said. “Tell me about them.”

“When the first baby laughed for the first time,” said Peter, “the laugh broke into a thousand pieces. Every piece became a fairy. But every time a child says ‘I don't believe in fairies,’ a fairy falls down dead somewhere.”

Peter told her about Neverland. He lived there with the Lost Boys. They were boys who fell out of their prams when their nurses were not looking. Nobody came for them, so Peter took them to Neverland. They had no mother.

“Why did you come to our window?” asked Wendy.

“To listen to the stories,” said Peter. “None of the Lost Boys knows any stories. Wendy, come with me to Neverland! You can tell us stories and be our mother.”

Wendy wanted to go very much. “Can John and Michael come too?” she asked.

“If you like,” said Peter.

They woke the boys. John and Michael were very excited too. Peter taught them to fly.

“You just think lovely wonderful thoughts,” he explained, “and they lift you up into the air.”

It didn't work, of course. Then Peter blew some fairy dust on them. Now it worked! First Michael rose into the air, then John, then Wendy. They flew around the nursery, laughing.

At that moment, Nana started barking loudly in the yard. Mr and Mrs Darling heard her and ran home from the party. But they were too late. When they came into the nursery, the window was open and the beds were empty. Far away, over the roofs of London, four little figures were flying towards the stars.

They flew for many days, second to the right and straight on till morning. At last Peter pointed down. “There it is,” he said. “Neverland.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4. The Little House
chapters.text:
Neverland was an island in the sea. There was a forest, a lagoon with mermaids, a camp of Indians and a pirate ship. The pirates had a terrible captain. His name was James Hook. He had a big iron hook instead of his right hand.

“Peter cut off his hand in a fight,” Peter told the children, “and threw it to a crocodile. The crocodile liked it very much, and now it follows Hook everywhere, to eat the rest of him. But the crocodile swallowed a clock, so it goes tick-tock, tick-tock. When Hook hears the clock, he runs away.”

Tinker Bell was jealous of Wendy. She flew ahead of the children to the Lost Boys.

“Peter wants you to shoot the Wendy bird,” she lied.

One of the Lost Boys, Tootles, took his bow and arrow. He shot at Wendy, and she fell to the ground. When Peter arrived, he was very angry. He looked at Wendy. The arrow had hit the acorn button on her chain. It was a present from Peter. It saved her life!

Peter was so angry with Tinker Bell that he sent her away for a week.

The Lost Boys were sorry. They built a little house around Wendy with walls, a roof and a chimney made from Hook's old hat. When Wendy woke up, she was very happy.

“Wendy, please be our mother,” said the Lost Boys.

“All right,” said Wendy. “I'm going to try my best.”

They lived under the ground in a secret home. They got into it through hollow trees. Every evening, Wendy cooked for them, sewed their clothes and told them stories before bed. She was a very good mother, and the Lost Boys loved her.

chapters.title: Chapter 5. The Mermaids' Lagoon
chapters.text:
Days in Neverland were full of adventures. One of the best was on the Mermaids' Lagoon. The mermaids sat on a big rock called Marooners' Rock and combed their long hair. They were beautiful, but they were not friendly to Wendy.

One afternoon, the children were playing near the rock. Suddenly the sky became dark, and the water became cold. The mermaids jumped into the sea.

“Pirates!” shouted Peter.

A small boat came to the rock. In it there were two pirates, Smee and Starkey, and a prisoner. It was Tiger Lily, the brave daughter of the Indian chief. The pirates wanted to leave her on the rock. When the water came up, she was going to drown.

Peter was very clever. He could copy anybody's voice. He shouted in Hook's voice, “Let her go!”

The pirates were surprised, but they obeyed. They cut the ropes, and Tiger Lily swam away.

Then the real Captain Hook swam to the boat. “Where is the prisoner?” he asked.

“You told us to let her go,” said Smee.

Hook was very angry and very frightened. Who was talking in his voice? Then he understood. It was Peter Pan! There was a terrible fight on the rock. Hook hurt Peter with his iron hook, and the pirates went back to their ship. They heard the tick-tock of the crocodile, and Hook swam away fast.

Peter and Wendy were alone on the rock. They were both hurt and tired, and the water was coming up. Peter couldn't fly. Luckily, a big kite came by. Peter tied it to Wendy, and it carried her home. Then a bird came on her floating nest. Peter got into it, used his shirt as a sail and sailed home safely.

After that, the Indians were good friends of Peter and the Lost Boys.

chapters.title: Chapter 6. Captain Hook's Ship
chapters.text:
One evening, Wendy told the children a story about a mother. Her children flew away, but she always left the window open for them. Wendy suddenly felt sad.

“We must go home,” she said. “Our mother is waiting for us.”

John and Michael agreed. The Lost Boys wanted to come too, because they wanted a mother and a home. Peter didn't want to go. “I don't want to grow up,” he said. But he promised to help them.

That night, the pirates attacked the Indians who were guarding the home under the ground. When the children came out of the trees, the pirates caught them one by one. They tied them up and carried them to the pirate ship, the Jolly Roger. Only Peter stayed in the house. He was sleeping.

Captain Hook came down into the house quietly. Peter's medicine was on the table. Hook put some poison into it and went away.

Tinker Bell came to wake Peter. She told him about the children. Peter took his medicine, but Tink knew about the poison. She drank it first, to save him. Now she was dying. Her light was getting weaker and weaker.

“Tink,” cried Peter. “What can I do?”

“I can get well,” she whispered, “if children believe in fairies.”

Peter stood up and called to all the children in the world who were dreaming about Neverland. “Do you believe in fairies? If you believe, clap your hands! Don't let Tink die!”

Many children clapped. Some didn't, but most of them did. Slowly, Tinker Bell's light became brighter again. She was saved!

“And now to rescue Wendy!” said Peter. He took his knife and flew to the pirate ship.

chapters.title: Chapter 7. Home Again
chapters.text:
On the Jolly Roger, the children were standing in a line. Wendy was tied to the mast. Captain Hook was very happy.

“Now, my boys,” he said, “you can become pirates, or you can walk the plank into the sea.”

“We are never going to be pirates!” shouted John.

Suddenly they heard a sound. Tick-tock, tick-tock. Hook fell on his knees and hid his face. “The crocodile!” he cried. “Hide me!”

But it was not the crocodile. It was Peter. He was making the tick-tock sound. He climbed onto the ship quietly and got into the captain's cabin. Soon he freed the children, and a great fight started. The Lost Boys fought bravely, and the pirates jumped into the sea one after another.

At last only Hook and Peter were left. They fought for a long time. Then Peter kicked Hook, and Hook fell into the sea. The real crocodile was waiting for him there with its mouth open. That was the end of Captain Hook.

Then Peter became the captain of the Jolly Roger. They sailed and flew back to London.

In London, the window of the nursery was still open. Mrs Darling was sitting sadly by the fire. Mr Darling was so sorry about Nana that he lived in her dog house. The children flew in quietly and got into their beds. When Mrs Darling saw them, she cried with happiness.

The Darlings adopted all the Lost Boys, too. Now they had a family and a home.

Peter didn't stay. “I don't want to go to school and become a man,” he said. But he promised to come back every spring. Wendy grew up and had a daughter, Jane. And one spring night, Peter came again to the window, and Jane flew away with him to Neverland. And so it goes on, as long as children are young and brave.
